sentences.text: Honeybees live together in a hive, and most of them are workers.
A worker bee flies from flower to flower and drinks a sweet liquid called nectar.
She carries the nectar back inside her body.
At the hive, she passes it to other bees.
They store it in small wax rooms called cells.
Then the bees fan the nectar with their wings.
The fanning helps water dry out of the nectar.
What is left is thick and sweet. That food is honey.
Bees eat the honey when flowers are hard to find.
A queen bee lays the eggs, but the workers are the ones who make the honey.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: Why queen bees build wax crowns
How worker bees turn nectar into honey

questions.explanation: The passage follows nectar from flowers into the hive, through fanning, until it becomes honey. That process is the main idea.

questions.prompt: In this passage, nectar means what?

choices.text: The wax walls of the hive
A kind of egg laid by workers

questions.explanation: The passage says a worker drinks a sweet liquid called nectar from flowers. That sentence tells the meaning in context.

choices.text: Bees fan the nectar with their wings
The nectar is stored in wax cells
Bees eat honey when flowers are scarce
A worker bee drinks nectar from flowers

questions.explanation: The worker collects nectar before it is passed on, stored, or fanned. Eating the honey comes last, when flowers are hard to find.
